chapter: Liberty Band, marriage and the Depression
title: His marriage in 1923 and the death of his sister Ethel Vinson
summary: He recalls marrying in 1923, going to Mexico in 1926, and the sudden death of his sister Ethel Vinson after a job.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I said what year you got married?

I said what year you got married? What year you got married? I think I got married in 1923. We went to Mexico in 1926. Ask him who he was playing with when he got married. I said who was playing with you when you got married? I said let me see. I think we had a new Liberty Bell band when I first got married. No, no, no. That's when my younger sister died. We had the old Liberty Bell. Maurice is what it's done. I was with my sister far by her. She had a beat. I was told I wasn't born when I got married. I told I wasn't born. Then sometimes we used to make up bands. We all get together. We hustle work. We hire one another. I hire old friends like that.
Ask him who, ask him what year his sister died.

What year your sister died? I'm not sick. I'm dying. What is that? I'm 19… Oh, I'm 19… Oh, I'm 19… 21, 19, 22. I'm 19. Because she used to take care of all my calls over the farm. And I started to sign up a job over the farm. And she told me that was her last job. The last time that she was gone. Help me out because she was gone. Next day she died. Uh… Uh… How suddenly…
Uh… What was her name? Ethel Vinson. Ethel…
